tldr: Headlines across all 13 country buckets frame the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia as an acute security emergency — 'war expands,' 'worst attack in years,' and 'largest attack' signal escalation risk — while roughly a third of titles name oil or energy facilities explicitly; the Bab al-Mandab strategic angle and war-economy consequences visible in body text are entirely absent from the headline layer.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline omitting 'Iran-backed' — frames the strikes as Houthi retaliation for Saudi military operations, invisibilising Iranian sponsorship at the title layer.
Only headline simultaneously naming US strikes on Iranian tankers alongside the Houthi-Saudi exchange, advertising the conflict as a multi-actor regional war rather than a bilateral proxy attack.
Only headline naming a third country's formal condemnation — India's diplomatic stance is signalled at the RSS/homepage layer, visible to readers before they click.
Only headline covering Saudi Arabia lifting the Khamis Mushait civil-defence alert — the sole de-escalation signal in the headline layer across 20 articles.

bottom_line: The headline layer universally advertises a security emergency while roughly a third of front pages also foreground oil-site damage, but the maritime chokepoint stakes, war-economy consequences, and humanitarian depth that appear in body text are entirely invisible at title level — readers who stop at headlines see a discrete strike event, not a widening multi-front war.
